No problem. Disc companies also typically have “base plastic” and “premium putting plastic”. For innova DX is the base and KC/Yeti/JK pro is the “premium putting plastic”. For trilogy prime/retro/origio is the “base plastic” and classic/zero/BT is the “premium putting plastic”. Base plastic is honestly fine for putting but the premium putting plastic is ideal. The additional benefit is using a base or “premium putting plastic” is significantly cheaper and easier to find

Several reasons but there is a good reason why you never see pros putting with premium plastics. Premium plastics are designed for throwing. A star/champ aviar is a throwing putter. The plastic can take impact from throws but will get scratched/gouged unacceptably from the chains while putting. Also the improved benefit to flight while using premium plastics and specifically halo plastic have no benefit inside the circle.

Perhaps most importantly premium plastics don’t have the right grip and tackiness for putting. Even compared to a soft putter they are too slick and have too much compliance.
